results.title: How to Grow Healthy Roses in Pots 🌹 | A Masterclass for Thriving Potted Roses
results.description:
If you’ve ever grown roses in pots and found them weak, lacklustre or constantly struggling — this video is for you.

In this masterclass, I take you step-by-step through how I grow strong, healthy, disease-resistant roses in containers — and why most potted roses fail.

🌱 Why compost alone isn’t enough

🌱 Cation exchange capacity explained simply

🌱 The role of soil biology and microbes

🌱 Feeding from above with organic matter

results.title: September Rose Care: 7 Things You MUST Do to Prepare for Winter
results.description:
Before you prune, feed, or cover your roses this September, check what they actually need. Autumn rose care begins with understanding your soil, your plants, and the weather ahead. In this video, James Scott from Golden Age Gardening explains seven practical care steps to help you prepare your roses for the colder months without creating unnecessary work.
Start with a simple soil check. Cooler afternoons and damp leaves do not always mean the roots have enough moisture. Learn why established roses, newly planted roses, and plants sheltered from rainfall may need different watering decisions, even when they grow in the same garden.
Next, explore how to keep healthy foliage while clearing infected fallen leaves. We discuss looking closely at damage, recognizing patterns, and avoiding treatments chosen without understanding the problem. Thoughtful cleanup can make your autumn routine more useful without leaving every rose bare.
Feeding and pruning also deserve careful timing. This guide explains why another fertilizer application may not solve yellowing leaves, how your expected frost period affects feeding decisions, and why securing a healthy cane can sometimes be more useful than cutting it off. Climbers, shrub roses, and other rose types do not all need the same treatment.
You will also learn what to check before adding mulch, why potted roses need their own winter plan, and how to prepare protection materials without installing them too early. From checking drainage holes to inspecting supports and loosening tight ties, small jobs can make seasonal care easier to manage.
This routine is intended for gardens moving into autumn and winter. If September brings spring where you live, or freezing weather is still months away, your roses will need a different seasonal schedule.
Take the work one plant at a time. Check the soil, collect diseased debris, preserve useful growth, and plan heavier jobs around local conditions.
Do your roses grow in pots or in the ground? Tell us when frost usually arrives in your area. Subscribe to Golden Age Gardening for straightforward advice that helps you care for your garden with confidence and a manageable workload.

results.title: 7 October Rose Care Mistakes That Could Ruin Next Year's Blooms
results.description:
🌹 **7 October Rose Care Mistakes That Could Ruin Next Year's Blooms!** Are you making these common fall rose care mistakes without realizing it? What you do to your roses in October can affect their winter survival, spring growth, and next year's beautiful flowers.

In this video, discover **7 important October rose care mistakes** that American gardeners should avoid before winter arrives.

Whether you're growing hybrid tea roses, climbing roses, shrub roses, grafted roses, or roses in containers, understanding the right autumn care is essential for healthy plants and beautiful blooms next season.

🍂 **YOU'LL DISCOVER:**

🌹 **Mistake #1:** Leaving black-spotted rose leaves on the ground and increasing the risk of disease returning next spring.

🌹 **Mistake #2:** Confusing rose rosette disease with ordinary red new growth and overlooking a serious rose virus.

🌹 **Mistake #3:** Cutting back climbing roses at the wrong time and removing the canes responsible for future flowers.

🌹 **Mistake #4:** Continuing to deadhead roses too late in cold climates instead of allowing their seasonal transition.

🌹 **Mistake #5:** Failing to protect the graft union, allowing winter damage to threaten your favorite rose variety.

🌹 **Mistake #6:** Ignoring tall rose canes and loose climbing supports that can contribute to wind damage.

🌹 **Mistake #7:** Leaving container roses exposed to winter temperatures without protecting their vulnerable root systems.

✅ **OCTOBER ROSE CARE FOR USDA ZONES 3–10**

Rose care is not the same everywhere in America. Gardeners in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Florida, and California face different autumn and winter conditions.

This guide explains why your USDA hardiness zone, rose variety, and local frost conditions matter when preparing roses for winter.

You'll also learn when to stop deadheading, how to recognize rose black spot, why climbing rose canes matter, how grafted roses can lose their original variety, and how to protect potted roses through winter.

results.description:
Picture your favorite rose in late April. The snow is gone, you expect to see red buds swelling, and instead the canes are dark, shriveled, and brittle. Most of the time, the cause isn’t something you did in January. It’s something that was skipped in October and November, before the first hard freeze arrived.

In this video, we walk through the full winter prep routine for roses, in the order that makes the most sense. That includes the one job most gardeners skip, which may matter more than any covering you can buy, and one popular protection product that can do more harm than good.
